title: Closest Subsequence Sum
statement: You get an integer array `nums` and an integer `goal`. Choose any subsequence of `nums`, meaning any collection of its elements (keeping or dropping each one independently, so choosing none or all is allowed), and let `sum` be the total of the chosen elements; an empty choice has `sum = 0`. Return the smallest value of `abs(sum - goal)` that some choice achieves.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every subsequence costs 2^40 sums, far too many. Meet in the middle splits `nums` into two halves of about 20 elements each and enumerates the 2^20 subset totals of each half separately. Any subsequence is one choice from the left half plus one from the right, so the question becomes: which pair `left[i] + right[j]` lands closest to `goal`? After sorting both lists, two pointers from opposite ends answer that in one linear sweep.

## Approach

1. `sumsOf` fills `sums` with every subset total of a half: for element `k`, the totals already built (`size = 2^k` of them) are copied with `part[k]` added. Then it sorts them.
2. Build sorted `left` and `right` lists for the two halves.
3. Start `best` at `abs(goal)`, the empty choice. Put `i` at the start of `left` and `j` at the end of `right`.
4. Look at `sum = left[i] + right[j]` and keep the smallest `abs(sum - goal)`.
5. If `sum` is too small, move `i` up; if too big, move `j` down; if exact, return `0`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [5, -7, 3, 5]`, `goal = 6`. The left half `[5, -7]` gives sorted totals `[-7, -2, 0, 5]`; the right half `[3, 5]` gives `[0, 3, 5, 8]`. Start with `i` on `-7` and `j` on `8`: total `1` is too small, so `i` moves to `-2`, total `6` equals the goal, and the answer is `0`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(2^(n/2) · n): building and sorting each list of 2^(n/2) totals dominates; the sweep is linear.
- Space: O(2^(n/2)) for the two lists.

## Pitfalls

- The empty subsequence counts, so `abs(goal)` is always achievable.
- A full 2^n enumeration times out at n = 40; split the array first.
- Sort numerically: a plain `Array.prototype.sort` compares as strings (the typed array here sorts by value).
- The closest total may lie just below or just above `goal`, so measure the distance at every pair the sweep visits, not only where it crosses the goal.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sumsOf` | builds the sorted subset totals of one half |
| `sums`, `size`, `mask` | totals so far, how many exist before element `k`, and the one being extended |
| `left`, `right` | sorted subset totals of the first and second half |
| `best` | smallest distance to `goal` seen |
| `i`, `j` | pointers into `left` (rising) and `right` (falling) |
| `sum` | total of the current pair |
